title: Astrocyte-derived CXCL14 promotes oligodendrocyte differentiation and remyelination via ERK1/2 signaling: implications for multiple sclerosis therapeutics
title_zh: 星形胶质细胞来源的CXCL14通过ERK1/2信号通路促进少突胶质细胞分化与再髓鞘化：对多发性硬化治疗的启示
abstract: Abstract Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a debilitating demyelinating disease of the central nervous system (CNS) in which progressive neurological disability is closely linked to the failure of endogenous remyelination. Reactive astrocytes are hallmarks of MS lesions, yet their functional role in myelin repair remains incompletely understood. Here, we report a pro-regenerative role for reactive astrocytes and demonstrate that their sustained activation during the remyelination phase is essential for oligodendrocyte (OL) precursor cell (OPC) differentiation and myelin repair in a cuprizone (CPZ)-induced demyelination mouse model. Reanalysis of a single-cell transcriptomic atlas combined with in situ immunostaining further revealed the selective upregulation of chemokine C-X-C motif ligand 14 (CXCL14) in reactive astrocytes during remyelination—a finding corroborated in lysolecithin (LPC) mouse model and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a neuroinflammatory demyelination model. In vitro, CXCL14 directly drives OPC differentiation into mature OLs by activating the extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1 and 2 (ERK1/2)-mediated mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway, which is independent of its effects on OPC survival or proliferation. Notably, astrocyte‑specific Cxcl14 knockdown abolished the pro‑differentiation activity of reactive astrocyte‑conditioned medium (ACM) in vitro and concurrently impaired remyelination in both the CPZ mouse model and EAE. Our findings reveal novel astrocyte–OPC crosstalk in pro-remyelination driven by CXCL14-dependent ERK1/2 signaling, highlighting CXCL14 as a promising therapeutic target for demyelinating diseases such as MS.
abstract_zh: 摘要 多发性硬化（MS）是一种中枢神经系统（CNS）的破坏性脱髓鞘疾病，进展性神经功能障碍与内源性再髓鞘化失败密切相关。活化星形胶质细胞是MS病灶的标志，但其在髓鞘修复中的功能作用尚未完全阐明。本文报道了活化星形胶质细胞的促再生作用，并证明其在再髓鞘化阶段持续激活对于少突胶质前体细胞（OPC）分化和髓鞘修复至关重要，使用铜胺（CPZ）诱导的脱髓鞘小鼠模型进行验证。对单细胞转录组图谱的重新分析结合原位免疫染色进一步揭示了在再髓鞘化期间活化星形胶质细胞中特异性上调的趋化因子C‑X‑C基序配体14（CXCL14）——这一发现亦在溶磷脂（LPC）小鼠模型和实验性自身免疫性脑脊髓炎（EAE）这一神经炎症性脱髓鞘模型中得到证实。体外实验显示，CXCL14通过激活细胞外信号调节激酶1/2（ERK1/2）介导的丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）信号通路，直接驱动OPC分化为成熟少突胶质细胞，该作用与其对OPC存活或增殖的影响无关。值得注意的是，星形胶质细胞特异性敲低Cxcl14消除了活化星形胶质细胞条件培养基（ACM）在体外的促分化活性，并同时削弱了CPZ小鼠模型和EAE中的再髓阘化。我们的研究揭示了星形胶质细胞与OPC之间通过CXCL14‑依赖的ERK1/2信号通路驱动的促再髓鞘化的新型细胞间通讯，强调CXCL14作为治疗脱髓鞘疾病（如MS）的有前景的靶点。
